notes:
Lead profile: early-stage SMB (customer support SaaS) — wants to add an AI assistant for in-app help and knowledgebase search. Mostly self-serve -> prefers hosted API. Key discussion points: model selection among Llama / Mistral / Qwen variants, and how to balance cost vs answer quality.

Customer technical constraints and preferences:
- Primary workload: support-agent + doc-search (short-turn interactive, <2s latency target for UI).
- Expected traffic: 30-60 concurrent chat sessions peak; average request length ~120 tokens; responses ~80 tokens.
- Cost sensitivity: critical — target monthly inference spend under $4k for pilot (est. 1-2M tokens / month).
- Prefers smaller models for most queries (7B-class) and higher-quality fallback for complex queries (14B-class) to control unit cost.
- Wants streaming responses and function calling for structured retrieval.

Model selection discussion (notes from demo & technical Q&A):
- Emberhill engineering asked about Llama-2/3 style 7B vs 13B variants: "Can we get acceptable quality on 7B if we prompt-engineer/chain-of-thought offloaded to retrieval?"
- Interest in Mistral-Instruct 7B for cheaper baseline; curiosity about 7B distilled Qwen for latency wins.
- Concern: hallucination on smaller models when KB coverage incomplete -> want clear fallback policy to a stronger 14B or hosted 3rd-party endpoint.
- Asked about Redwood Optimize: automated batching suggestions + quantization profiles — helpful for cost targets.

Preliminary bench results shared by Emberhill (internal):
- Mistral-7B: avg token latency 12ms/token on hosted trial, cost est ~ $0.9k/month at their volume (good).
- Qwen-14B: avg token latency 28ms/token, cost est ~ $3.6k/month; noticeably better answer quality on enterprise KB queries in their eval set.
- Llama-13B variants: quality similar to Qwen-14B in some prompts but cost/latency between the two.

Customer quotes and tone:
- CTO (A. Rivera): "We need production-like numbers — not just cherry-picked demos. If the 7B baseline works 80% of the time, fallback should be seamless and cheap."
- Product lead: "Self-serve is ideal — we want to spin up a PoC same week and show metrics to ops."

Open items / asks from Emberhill:
- Request: a two-column matrix (cost per 1k tokens vs expected QA score for their prompt set) for Llama/Mistral/Qwen family variants.
- Request: short-lived PoC API key + instructions for running batch eval harness (we recommended Redwood sample harness and offered a starter prompt set).
- Security: they need SOC2 report and SSO integration docs before pilot expands beyond dev team.

Next immediate actions (AE & SE):
- Provide tailored cost/latency matrix with Redwood-specific pricing and recommended quantization profiles.
- Issue PoC key restricted to their trial org; include example curl/SDK calls and starter prompt templates tuned for retrieval-augmented queries.
- Offer 30m benchmarking session with SE to run side-by-side Llama-7B vs Mistral-7B vs Qwen-14B on their prompt sample.

CRM style summary (short):
- SMB inbound, public cloud preferred, early discovery. Main blocker is model selection tradeoff (quality vs cost) + SOC2 docs. Good fit for hosted_api + optimize guidance. Likely convert to small monthly commit if PoC shows clear cost savings and acceptable fallback quality.
